subject_line: Urban trees and rural birds in Siteseeing
email_body:
Dear Ariel,

I was struck by how Siteseeing began: you writing about Winnipeg's urban trees and Brenda Schmidt about rural Saskatchewan birds, with the back-and-forth gradually turning into a book about place itself. That thread runs back through TreeTalk and Treed, and now into your year as Writer-in-Residence at the Winnipeg Public Library.

I would love to ask how a collaboration across two provinces changed the way you look at a single tree, and what residency conversations with local writers have taught you.

Dear Elliott,

I came across Grey Dog through its shortlisting for the Edmund White Award for Debut Fiction and the Kobo Emerging Writer Prize, and through a Publishers Weekly starred review that called the prose as sharp as a scalpel. I also noticed you spoke about the novel on CTV Atlantic in May 2025.

I would love to ask what the year after a debut has looked like from Halifax, and which scene in Grey Dog took you longest to get right.

subject_line: Seeing home freshly in Album Rock
email_body:
Dear Matthew,

I noticed that your work moves between poetry and photography, from Optic Nerve with Brick Books to Album Rock with Boulder Books, and that Monica Kidd's review in Newfoundland Quarterly praised how you see your own home in a fresh way. Your 2020 CBC Poetry Prize win was also how I first heard your name.

I would love to ask how the camera and the line break shape each other when you write about St. John's and Ktaqmkuk.

subject_line: Halifax's ninth poet laureate and Body Parts
email_body:
Dear Anna,

I read that you were named Halifax's ninth Poet Laureate in April 2024, with a term running to 2027, and that your chapbook Body Parts came out with Gaspereau Press in 2021.

I would love to ask what the laureateship has asked of your writing so far: whether public occasions have pulled your poems in new directions, and what you hope to leave with the city by the end of the term.
